title: TesseraQL Simple YAML v1 — shared definitions
description: Definitions the per-kind document schemas share. `shared` holds the keys more than one kind declares identically - the envelope (version, id) and the acquisition and file-transfer keys a route and a job author the same way; the rest are the value shapes every kind refers to. Referenced by relative $ref from the sibling schema files, so one declaration serves every kind.
$comment: Not a document schema: nothing validates against this file directly.

id.description: Unique document id, e.g. products.page; referenced by tests, coverage, governance approvals, and logs.

input.description: Declared input fields - one contract for routes and jobs alike (a job's parameters bind and validate exactly like a route's). Documented in app-layout.md and jobs.md.

datasource.description: The named connector under tesseraql.datasources the route's SQL runs on, defaulting to main. The name must be declared (TQL-YAML-1035); a non-main route cannot declare notify:/publish:/outbox: or sequence allocation - they ride the main connector (TQL-YAML-1036).

format.description: The tabular format the uploaded file is parsed as. `csv` is built in; `excel` needs the tesseraql-excel module (TQL-LD-2801 when the codec is absent).

columns.description: How the file's columns map to the per-row statement's bind names. Omit it to use the header labels as bind names.

headerRow.description: Whether the table starts with a header row (default `true`). With a header, simple-form columns match by label rather than by position.

startRow.description: The 1-based row the table starts at, for files carrying title rows above the data (default 1).

sheet.description: For workbook formats, the sheet to read (default: the first).

locale.description: The locale `type:`/`format:` columns parse dates and numbers in. A literal, or a request source such as `principal.claim.locale`; unset, `tesseraql.files.locale` applies.

onError.description: What a failing row does: `rollback` (default) fails the whole import, `skip` records the row and commits the rest. Either way the rejected rows are reported with their row numbers.

import.description: file-import parsing and column-to-bind mapping (headerRow, startRow, columns, onError: rollback|skip). It says how to parse, never what to write: the per-row statement is the document's one steps:/pipeline: entry. Documented in file-transfers.md.

format.description: The format the rows are written as. `csv` is built in; `excel` and `pdf` need their modules (TQL-LD-2801 when the codec is absent).

filename.description: The download filename, defaulting to the document id plus the format's extension. `{dotted.path}` interpolates a context value, and a `splitBy:` export must carry `{key}`.

template.description: A workbook or print template colocated with the document: an .xlsx for excel, an .html for pdf. A path that does not exist fails the build rather than quietly writing a plain grid.

sheet.description: For workbook formats, the sheet to write.

startCell.description: Placement mode: where data rows start in the template, e.g. `B5`. Refused without a template (TQL-YAML-1041), and refused on pdf (TQL-YAML-1005) — a page lays out through its template, not through cell positions.

columns.description: The columns written, in order, with their headings and format patterns. Omit it to write every column the rows carry, under its own name.

locale.description: The locale date and number patterns render in. A literal, or a request source such as `principal.claim.locale`, so the requesting user decides; unset, `tesseraql.files.locale` applies. A job has no request, so a step's is a literal.

timezone.description: The zone date and time values render in, with the same literal / request-source / `tesseraql.files.timezone` fallback as `locale`.

timing.description: `extract` (default) runs the statement in the extraction's transaction, so rows are marked exactly when they are extracted; `download` runs it once on the first successful file fetch. A job's export step supports `extract` only (TQL-YAML-1041).

sql.description: The follow-up statement, written as a source's `sql:` arm is — `file:`, `params:`, and the rest of the arm's keys.

after.description: A statement run once after the extraction, typically to mark the extracted rows. `file-export` only: on `query-export` it is a build error (TQL-CAMEL-3101), because a synchronous download has no transaction to hang it on.

maxRows.description: The ceiling for a format that holds every row before it writes (pdf, and the workbook template modes), defaulting to `tesseraql.resultMaterialization.maxRows`; a negative value opts out. A streaming format is never capped.

onOverflow.description: `fail` (default) refuses an export past `maxRows` (TQL-LD-2850); `warn` truncates it at the cap and logs.

groupBy.description: A column the rows are read as ordered groups by, each exposed to the template as a `key` and its own `rows`. The rows must be ordered by it (TQL-LD-2851).

splitBy.description: A column that splits the export into one document per value, delivered as a single ZIP; `filename:` must carry `{key}`. The rows must be ordered by it (TQL-LD-2851).

export.description: query-export / file-export output: format (csv, excel, pdf), filename, columns with headers and format patterns, locale/timezone. It says how the rows are written and never what to read - the rows come from sources.main on a route, or the step's own arm in a pipeline. Documented in file-transfers.md.

on.description: The join: each column of the rows being enriched to the column of the reference it matches. Several pairs make a composite key, compared by the framework's canonical normalization (INTEGER 1 matches BIGINT 1).

sql.description: Fetch the reference by key, written as a source's `sql:` arm is. The statement must bind `keys` — one that never mentions it reads the whole table once per batch and still returns the right answer, which is why only the build can catch it (TQL-YAML-1048).

http.description: Call the reference by key, written as a source's `http:` arm is, plus `select:` and `onError:`. How the keys reach it is `mode:`.

source.description: A result already in the context, joined without a fetch, named by its context path: a route source by name, a job step as `steps.<id>`. A spooled sibling is refused (TQL-CAMEL-3114) — load it into a table and enrich from there.

mode.description: For an `http:` reference: `perRow` (default) makes one request per distinct key, `batch` one request per `batchSize` keys. A `sql:` reference is always batched — a statement takes a key list by construction.

as.description: Attach the matched rows as a list under this name. Exactly one of `as:` or `merge:` (TQL-YAML-1047).

merge.description: Copy these columns of the matched row onto each row instead of attaching a list. Exactly one of `as:` or `merge:` (TQL-YAML-1047).

batchSize.description: How many distinct keys one fetch carries.

maxKeys.description: The ceiling on distinct keys collected for one enrichment, past which the reference is refused rather than read unboundedly.

enrichment.description: One keyed reference folded into a binding's rows: where the keys are (`on:`), what answers them (`sql:`, `http:` or `source:` — exactly one), and how the answer lands (`as:` or `merge:`). Documented in lookups.md.

channel.description: The declared channel this notification is enqueued on, which decides the transport (mail, webhook, queue) and its configuration. It must exist (TQL-FIELD-2004).

when.description: A core expression over the result context; the notification is enqueued only when it holds, so a conditional send is a declaration rather than a branch.

recipient.description: A bindable path resolving to the address this notification goes to, overriding the channel's configured recipients.

attach.description: A bindable path resolving to a transfer id — typically an export step's `steps.<id>.transferId` — whose file rides along. Mail channels only (TQL-FIELD-2004).

payload.description: Each payload key to the bindable path supplying its value; the template or transport reads them by name.

delay.description: Hold this entry back this long after the commit, e.g. `72h`. Exclusive with deliverAt: (TQL-BATCH-5317). Documented in notifications.md.

deliverAt.description: Hold this entry back until the instant this bindable path resolves to. Exclusive with delay: (TQL-BATCH-5317). Documented in notifications.md.

cancelKey.description: A bindable path whose value this entry is filed under, so a later command can withdraw it while it is still undelivered. Documented in notifications.md.

cancel.description: A bindable path naming the cancelKey to withdraw: this block withdraws undelivered entries instead of writing one, in the withdrawing command's own transaction. Declared instead of channel:, never beside it.

notification.description: One notification enqueued on the transactional outbox, so it is sent if and only if the write commits. Documented in notifications.md.

transport.description: Where the file goes: `local` writes under the work directory, `sftp`/`ftps` reach an allow-listed remote host.

host.description: The remote server, which must be allow-listed under `tesseraql.connectors.push.hosts`. Required on a remote transport (TQL-YAML-1042).

port.description: The remote port, defaulting to the transport's.

path.description: The destination directory. The file is staged and renamed into place, so a poller on the far side never reads a partial file.

credential.description: The named credential under `tesseraql.connectors.push.credentials`. Required on a remote transport (TQL-YAML-1042).

file.description: A bindable path resolving to the transfer id of the file to deliver, typically an earlier export step's `steps.<id>.transferId`.

as.description: The name the file lands under, defaulting to the transfer's own filename. `{dotted.path}` interpolates a context value.

push.description: Delivery of a produced transfer to a local or remote drop — the outbound mirror of the poll trigger, under the same policy block. Documented in file-transfers.md.

reader.description: What the loop reads, a window at a time: its own `sql:`, or `spool:` naming an earlier step's spool. A chunk step's work is its reader and writer, so the step declares no arm of its own (TQL-FIELD-2004).

writer.description: What runs for each row the reader produced, binding that row's columns.

key.description: The reader column checkpoints track, defaulting to `id`. A restart resumes after the last committed key, which is why the reader must be ordered by it.

commitEvery.description: How many rows one committed slice holds. A checkpoint lands with each commit, so this is also how much a restart repeats.

onError.description: `fail` (default) fails the step on the first writer error; `skip` records the row in `tql_job_skips` and continues, up to `skipLimit`.

skipLimit.description: How many skipped rows the step tolerates before failing anyway, so a systematically broken load does not run to completion looking fine.

enrich.description: Keyed references folded into each window before the writer sees it, so a writer may bind a column the reader's query never selected. A reference failure fails the window, not the row.

batch.description: `true` executes the writer in JDBC batches of `commitEvery` rows — one round trip per committed slice instead of one per row. Requires the default `onError: fail`: a batch cannot attribute a member failure to one row, so a failure fails the chunk, which reruns from its last checkpoint. Documented in jobs.md.

chunk.description: Restartable per-row processing: a reader, a writer, and committed checkpoints, so a job that stops resumes where it left off instead of starting over. Documented in jobs.md.

name.description: The bind name on import, the row column on export. The simple form `- name` is this key and nothing else.

label.description: The heading in the file — the same word a view column uses, and a message key resolves through the app bundles. Defaults to `name`.

column.description: An explicit position instead of matching by header: a column letter (`D`) or a 1-based number.

type.description: Parses the file's text into a typed bind on import, and writes a typed cell on export. Omit it for plain text.

format.description: The parse/render pattern the `type:` uses, e.g. `yyyy/MM/dd` or `#,##0.00` — and, for workbooks, the matching cell format.

fileColumn.description: One column of a file transfer, in either form: the bare name, or an object adding the file-side heading, an explicit position, and a type with its pattern. Documented in file-transfers.md.

domain.description: Name of a field domain declared under domains/; its type, bounds, pattern, format, enum, classification and mask merge in, and the keys declared here win. Operational keys (required, requiredWhen, default, writable) stay route-local.

description.description: What this field is, in the words a caller reads. A wire field on both MCP surfaces derived from input: an mcp/ prompt's argument carries it in prompts/list, and an mcp/ tool's inputSchema carries it as the JSON Schema description a model follows. Declarable on a domain, and inherited from one.

type.description: The declared type. A supplied value is coerced to it and refused when it does not fit. `sort` is an ordered sort set (`-ship,order` - a leading `-` for descending) validated against `columns:`; the bound `params.<name>Sql` sibling carries the safe ORDER BY fragment.

required.description: Refuse the request when this field is absent.

default.description: The value bound when the request omits the field.

pattern.description: Anchored regular expression (TQL-YAML-1012 when it does not compile).

columns.description: The sortable-column allowlist a `type: sort` input validates its keys against; required for that type and legal on no other.

format.description: string: email|uuid|url; date/number: a parse pattern.

enum.description: The accepted values; anything else is refused.

writable.description: `false` makes the field read-only: it renders in a derived form but is never bound from the request.

classification.description: Data classification label carried into masking and audit. Documented in data-scoping.md.

mask.description: The masking rule applied when the principal may not see the value.

widget.description: Presentation hint (docs/declarative-views.md): the form widget this field renders as, declared once on a domain; a per-view fields: override wins. Never part of the HTTP contract.

codes.description: The code catalog this field's values come from (docs/lookups.md): the binder accepts only that catalog's active codes, and the violation is the enum field error. Declared on a domain, so the value set has one home instead of an enum that drifts from the master.

policy.description: Write authorization (docs/declarative-views.md): a security policy the principal must satisfy to supply this field; a failing principal's value follows the route's readOnly behavior, and the derived form omits the field. Operational — never accepted inside a domain.

type.description: The element type, for an array of scalars. Mutually exclusive with fields: (TQL-YAML-1027).

enum.description: The accepted element values; anything else is refused.

fields.description: The element's own fields, for an array of objects — the header-plus-lines shape a business form submits. Elements bind, coerce and validate exactly as top-level fields do, and a violation addresses itself by index (`lines[2].qty`). One level deep: an array inside an element is refused (TQL-YAML-1027). Documented in declarative-validation.md.

items.description: Element constraints for `type: array`: `type:`/`enum:` for scalar elements, `fields:` for object elements.

visible.description: `false` removes the field from the response entirely, for every caller.

policy.description: The security policy a principal must satisfy to see the value unmasked.

mask.description: The masking rule applied when the policy is not satisfied, such as showing only the last four characters.

classification.description: Data classification label carried into audit. Documented in data-scoping.md.

unmaskWhen.description: An expression that, when it matches, reveals the value despite the mask.

when.description: A whitelist-only expression over the execution context; the first matching entry wins.

status.description: The HTTP status to answer when the expression is truthy.

file.description: A colocated 2-way SQL file, relative to the declaring document (must exist; TQL-SQL-2103). This arm's acquisition target, the role `url` plays for `http`.

mode.description: How the statement runs and what it binds: `query` (rows), `query-one` (a single row), `update` (an affected-row count), `query-spool` (rows streamed to a spool a later chunk: step reads, never held), or `call` (a stored call on a command step, its OUT parameters declared under `out:`).

params.description: Each bind name to the bindable path supplying its value, such as `path.id`, `params.unit` or `principal.claim.tenant_id`.

keys.description: Columns whose database-generated values are captured after an insert; they bind as `steps.<id>.keys.<column>`.

out.description: The OUT parameters of a `mode: call` statement on a command step: each name to its JDBC type keyword (varchar, numeric, integer, bigint, boolean, date, timestamp, double). The statement binds them as `out.<name>` bind sites and the values publish as `steps.<id>.out.<name>`. Documented in transactional-writes.md.

timeoutSeconds.description: Per-binding SQL statement timeout override; 0 disables. Default: tesseraql.sql.timeoutSeconds, else 30s.

datasource.description: The named connector this read runs on, overriding the document's. Legal on a read only: a batch step owns its own transaction so an extract elsewhere splits nothing, while a write on another connector would be a second transaction nothing owns (TQL-YAML-1037).

maxRows.description: Largest number of rows materialized. Default: `tesseraql.resultMaterialization.maxRows`.

onOverflow.description: `fail` (the default) refuses a result past `maxRows`; `warn` truncates it and logs.

materialize.description: Bounds on how much of the result is held in memory.

rowCount.description: The exact number of rows the statement must affect (rows is a list of records everywhere else).

onMismatch.description: `conflict` (the default) answers 409, so a stale edit is refused honestly; `error` answers 500.

expect.description: The row count this statement must affect, and what happens when it does not — the declarative optimistic-locking check on an update or delete.

sql.description: The SQL arm: a colocated 2-way SQL file and how it is run. The keys of the mechanism nest inside the arm that owns them, so there is nowhere to write a call's `select:` on a statement and no lint has to say it is wrong.

name.description: The named IAM SQL contract to execute instead of a colocated file, so an app reuses the identity schema's statements. Documented in authentication.md.

mode.description: How the contract runs and what it binds, exactly as it means on the `sql` arm.

params.description: Each bind name to the bindable path supplying its value, such as `path.id`, `params.unit` or `principal.claim.tenant_id`.

rowCount.description: The exact number of rows the statement must affect (rows is a list of records everywhere else).

onMismatch.description: `conflict` (the default) answers 409, so a stale edit is refused honestly; `error` answers 500.

expect.description: The row count this statement must affect, and what happens when it does not — the declarative optimistic-locking check on an update or delete.

contract.description: The contract arm: a statement the identity schema owns, called by name. It reads or writes like any other statement, so it carries the same `mode`, `params` and `expect`.

name.description: The named runtime service provider to call instead of running SQL (docs/extending.md): non-SQL runtime state (lanes, traces, file trees, …) read as rows.

params.description: Each bind name to the bindable path supplying its value, such as `path.id`, `params.unit` or `principal.claim.tenant_id`.

service.description: The service arm: a runtime provider answering rows from process state. It takes only its arguments — there is no statement to run, so no mode and no row-count expectation.

method.description: The HTTP method. Default GET; a source is not restricted to GET, because JSON-RPC, GraphQL and `POST …/search` batch lookups are reads.

url.description: The absolute http/https URL. Its host must be allow-listed under tesseraql.http.outbound.allowedHosts — egress is deny by default (TQL-SEC-4070).

headers.description: Static request headers; values may carry ${…} config or secret placeholders, resolved on send.

query.description: Query-string parameters, each a bindable path resolved against the execution context.

credential.description: A named credential the SecretResolver supplies at call time, so a document never carries a secret.

body.description: A bindable path whose value is serialized as the request body.

expectStatus.description: The exact status that counts as success; the default is any 2xx. A mismatch fails the call without tripping the circuit breaker — it is a deterministic rejection, not a sign the dependency is down.

connectTimeout.description: Connect timeout for this call (e.g. 2s), overriding tesseraql.http.outbound.connectTimeout.

requestTimeout.description: Request timeout for this call (e.g. 10s), overriding tesseraql.http.outbound.requestTimeout.

attempts.description: Total attempts including the first (TQL-YAML-1058 outside 1..10).

backoff.description: The wait before the second attempt, e.g. 200ms.

multiplier.description: The factor the wait grows by before each further attempt.

retry.description: Opt-in retry for transient faults: connect failures, timeouts and 5xx are repeated; a 4xx and an expectStatus mismatch never are. Unstated numbers come from tesseraql.http.outbound.retry. Every repeated attempt counts against the circuit breaker, the sequence ends the moment the host's circuit opens, and it lives inside a budget of attempts x requestTimeout. Documented in connectors.md.

select.description: A dotted path into the response JSON naming the part that becomes rows. Default: the whole body.

onError.description: `fail` (default) fails the request or step; `empty` degrades to zero rows and an `error` entry, and the page still renders. The degradation is logged and metered — it is not silent.

readOnly.description: The author's assertion that the call has no side effect, required on a command route: the write can roll back and the request cannot.

mode.description: How the acquired rows are delivered: `query` (default — held and published as rows) or `query-spool` (streamed to a spool a later chunk: step loads, so an API result can be written to the database without holding it). A call reads, so the SQL write modes are not modes it has.

http.description: The http arm: an outbound call whose response becomes this binding's rows, in the vocabulary every outbound call shares. Rides the outbound gateway — allow-listed hosts, named credentials, timeouts, and a per-host circuit breaker.

sequence.description: Allocate the next value of a managed document-number sequence instead of running a statement; it binds as `steps.<id>.value`. It has no body beyond its name, which is why it sits beside the arms rather than being one. Documented in transactional-writes.md.

spool.description: A context path resolving to an earlier step's spool reference (`steps.<id>.spool`), read as this binding's rows. A chunk reader declares it instead of `sql:` to load what another step extracted — from another connector, or from an API — because a spool is a spool whoever filled it. Documented in jobs.md.

when.description: Guard expression on a step: a falsy guard skips it, recording `steps.<id>.skipped` instead of a result. A guard is about whether the step runs at all, not a question for the mechanism, so it sits beside the arm. The declared branch point for decision.* outputs (docs decision-tables).

enrich.description: Keyed references folded into this binding's rows before anything reads them (docs/lookups.md), keyed by enrichment name and applied in authored order. An enrichment nests under the source it transforms, so any arm's rows can be enriched. Each entry names one reference — sql: (fetch by key), http: (call by key), or source: (a result already in the context, joined without a fetch, named by its context path: a route source by name, a job step as steps.<id>) — plus the on: join and one of as:/merge:. Only a binding that holds rows can carry one: a write publishes affectedRows, and a query-spool extract never held its rows.

binding.description: One acquisition or one statement. Exactly one mechanism arm names the means — sql (a colocated 2-way SQL file), contract (a named identity contract), service (a runtime provider), http (an outbound call) — or the write-side sequence, and that arm nests the keys the mechanism owns. Beside the arms sit the three questions no mechanism answers: the when: guard, the enrich: folded into the rows, and the spool: another step filled. Documented in unified-sources.md.
